spec.name: deep_to_surface_rms_ratio
spec.why: Deep currents are normally weaker than surface currents, so a ratio much less than 1 (practical threshold ~0.1) indicates physical behavior. It is scale-invariant: uniformly reducing forcing or viscosity lowers both numerator and denominator, so the metric cannot be 'gamed' by simply making the whole flow small. Flat or gently sloping bathymetry naturally gives a small ratio, while steep sigma-coordinate topography can generate spurious deep velocities, inflating the ratio and revealing numerical error.
